I farm in Quzhou County, Hebei, where the usual pattern is winter wheat followed by summer maize, and that is what I will do this year. I am 68, so I will keep to a simple, familiar system that matches my strength, my experience, and the local climate. I will plant improved winter wheat in autumn because it is stable, I know how to manage it, and it fits well with our land and water conditions. After harvesting wheat, I will plant summer maize, using hybrid seed because maize hybrids usually give me better yield and stronger growth. I will keep fertilizer use moderate and practical, not too heavy, because I want steady production without wasting money. I will use rotary tillage because it is easier and faster for me than deep ploughing, and I will arrange a few key irrigations for wheat and fewer for maize, since wheat in our area depends more on timely water. For pests and disease, I will spray only a limited number of times at the main risk periods, because I want to control problems but keep labor and cost manageable. My goal is not the highest possible yield, but a reliable harvest I can manage well myself.
